findings.text: Device managed pool creation rejects a duplicate named pool on the same device, optionally duplicates the supplied name, allocates a device resource holder, creates an underlying pool, records its name, attaches the holder, and returns the pool or an error pointer on failure.

Device tree pool lookup resolves a phandle at a property index, prefers the referenced device, otherwise falls back to the parent device plus a label or node name, then looks up the named pool on that device and balances node and device references.

Generic radix access provides non-allocating address lookup, allocating lookup that can consume and return a caller supplied spare node, bulk reservation over a byte range in node sized steps, recursive teardown, and atomic root detachment followed by recursive release.

Forward and backward radix iteration expose peek operations that translate an iterator offset into a leaf data address, skip absent child ranges by rounding the offset, maintain a page scaled position, use a maximum value sentinel for exhaustion, and clamp an out of range backward offset to the current tree extent.

Filename style matching exposes a null terminated predicate and a bounded length predicate, both pure and both delegating to a shared internal matcher that optionally treats a supplied end pointer as end of input.

CPU grouping exposes a NUMA aware allocator that spreads a requested group count over present then possible CPUs and reports how many masks were populated, plus a narrow fallback variant that places every possible CPU into only the first mask and reports one mask.
Hex conversion exposes a decoder from pairs of hex characters into bytes with validation and an encoder from bytes into hex characters that returns the advanced output position.

Public entry for balanced CPU masks takes a group count and an out count, returns null for zero groups or allocation failure, otherwise returns an array of masks sized by the request with the out count clamped to the request.

Glob and hex helpers are callable pure or side effect confined utilities: matching takes pattern and subject with optional length, decoding takes destination plus source and byte count, encoding takes destination plus source and count.
Node grouping record holds an identifier plus a union that is interpreted first as a CPU count for sorting and sizing and later as an assigned group count for that node or cluster.

Device managed pool creation preserves uniqueness per device and ordered cleanup: name duplication happens before resource allocation, pool creation happens before publication, and failures unwind in reverse order without publishing a partial pool.

Radix growth keeps enlarging depth until the requested offset fits under the depth capacity, prepends the old root as first child of a new node, tags depth into the root value, and publishes with an atomic compare exchange that retries on loss while clearing the losing spare link.

Descent indexes each level by shifting the remaining offset by the level capacity shift, masks it by the node size, atomically installs a missing child exactly once, reuses the loser spare, frees any unused spare, and finally returns the leaf slot for the residual offset.

Glob semantics treat question as any single non terminator, star as an arbitrary length sequence with trailing star as immediate success, bracket classes with ranges and leading exclamation negation plus literal closing bracket first, backslash escape for the next pattern symbol, and star as matching separators too.

Group sizing sorts nodes or clusters by CPU count ascending, assigns at least one group to every active participant using proportional share of remaining groups, clamps total groups to total CPUs, marks inactive participants with a sentinel, and asserts assigned groups never exceed local CPUs.

Per group CPU assignment distributes rounding remainder by giving one extra CPU to leading groups, wraps the group cursor at the end of the mask array, and fills each mask sibling first then node local CPUs, with an optional cluster aware pass used only when cluster count fits in the node group budget.

Node to CPU mapping is built by setting every possible CPU into its node mask, node membership of a target mask is computed by intersection, and the two stage spread snapshots present CPUs once so hotplug only moves a CPU between stages.

Hex decoding consumes two source characters per output byte, validates each nibble, and stops with an invalid argument failure without partial output guarantee; encoding emits exactly two output characters per input byte in order.

Radix access is lock free for readers and concurrent growers: root and child loads use one time reads, publication uses release compare exchange, teardown detaches the root with an atomic exchange, and no mutex or spin lock appears in the fragments.

Glob matching runs as a single star backtrack machine: it remembers only the most recent star and its starting subject position, and on mismatch rewinds the pattern there while advancing the subject by one, failing only when input ends or no star was seen.

Radix peek runs as descend or skip and restart: missing children advance or retreat the iterator by the subtree span and recompute position; overflow of the forward span parks the iterator at the exhaustion sentinel; running past the last slot at a level restarts from the reloaded root.

Allocation and lookup failures are signalled as null or negative errno error pointers: duplicate pool, missing name duplication, missing devres holder, missing pool, null radix node allocation, bulk reservation shortfall, null mask and node table allocation, and cluster table allocation all unwind already acquired resources.
Lowercase and uppercase hex digit tables each provide the sixteen ASCII symbols for nibble values zero through fifteen in ascending order.
